summary.text: Kut is made from jaggery or molasses in which scrap iron such as horseshoes and gram flour have been fermented for ten to fifteen days; the iron-water is mixed with tree gum.

citations.quote: Kut printing is usually undertaken in the afternoon.The kut is a smooth finer paste made from jaggery, or molasses, in which scrap iron such as horse-hoes and besan (gram flour) have been fermented for ten to fifteen days.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 6

citations.quote: The resulting liquid or “ironwater” is drained off and mixed with smooth tree gum paste.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 6
